newsitem.title: EGYPT: Strong milling shares give push to Egypt bourse.
newsitem.headline: Strong milling shares give push to Egypt bourse.

text.p: Strong activity in milling shares boosted Egyptian share prices on Wednesday, ending a week-long decline that was exacerbated by a new dealing system, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) overall index rose 0.4 points to close at 233.95 while turnover was a low 16.17 million pounds ($4.76 million).
"It's a good sign that the index is up, it means the market is stronger. But without the new dealing system it would be much better," said Youssef Khalil of Delta EAB Brokerage.
Milling shares dominated the day's trading, with Central and West Delta Flour Mills beating the bunch and ending 0.25 pounds higher at 53.50 after trade worth 2.48 million.
Popular Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed 0.15 pounds higher at 48.00 after trade worth almost two million pounds.
Recently privatised East Delta Flour Mills traded shares worth 1.44 million pounds but slipped 0.25 pounds to end at 39.50.
"The milling sector is the most successful on the market. Many shareholders expect millers to announce profits of about 20 percent next year," Khalil said.
Arab Cotton Ginning was the market leader, closing 1.00 pounds higher at 33.00 after trading shares worth almost two million pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 358.72 points from 357.45 on Tuesday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 162.68 from 162.57.
